verdict.rationale: llamafile bundles its own chat interfaces: a web chat UI served at localhost:8080 and a `--cli` mode that answers whatever you prompt, including image description via `/upload`. That gives users a built-in local assistant they can hand prompts to. There is no evidence of agentic delegation, meaning tool use, multi-step task execution or actions taken on the user's behalf; it is prompt-and-answer chat only. Missing for 10: agentic multi-step task execution, tool/action capabilities, documentation of delegation workflows, independent hands-on corroboration of task delegation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: you can also chat with it using [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp)'s Web UI: just open a browser window and connect to http://localhost:8080/
If you add the `--cli` argument to a llamafile, you will run a CLI version of the model that answers to whatever you provide as a prompt
you can also upload an image by using the `/upload` command and specifying the path to the image
The llamafile UX (CLI interface and web server with chat) is great
